assignment.objective: Investigate the mutation graph of sorted positive-integer solutions of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd under Vieta mutation. First prove or refute the structural claims — connectivity of every solution to (1,1,1,1), uniqueness of a height-decreasing mutation at every non-root vertex, and the consequent rooted-tree structure of the quotient graph — then pursue the open asymptotic part: strongest attainable rigorous upper and lower bounds for N(H), the relation between mutation depth and log H, an active search for exceptional small solutions, hidden cycles, multiple parents, and induction failure modes, and sharply separated conjectures. Deliver a self-contained research memorandum.
assignment.rationale: The named answers assemble the D10 memorandum. DEFINITIONS: sorted quadruples 1<=a<=b<=c<=d with a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd, Vieta mutation with re-sorting, height = max coordinate d, root (1,1,1,1), N(H) counts vertices with d<=H (restated from SC1-SC6, C3, C6 in each answer). PROVED: (D1) connectivity of every solution to (1,1,1,1) by strict integer height descent via d'=4abc-d; (D2) uniqueness of the height-decreasing mutation at every non-root, with the equal-coordinate subtlety resolved at the vertex level; (D3) the quotient mutation graph is a rooted tree (cycle/multiple-parent exclusion from D2 plus the no-height-preserving-mutation corollary) — answer:work:003-struct-core-v2. (D4) N(H) <= C*H^rho + O(log H) with rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582 and effective C <= 0.372, via the proved slow/fast dichotomy (the a=b=1 locus is a single chain with ratio -> 2+sqrt(3); ab is nondecreasing along child edges; off-chain subtrees rooted at u_j have per-edge factor >= 11 and m_j >= 121*(11/3)^{j-2}, making the subtree sum convergent); (D6) two-sided depth relation log_3(log_2 d + 1) <= depth(v) <= log_3 d, with the chain the unique slowest branch at depth log_{2+sqrt3}(d)+O(1) — answer:work:004-upper-depth-v3. (D5) N(H) >= max{floor(log_{2+sqrt3} H)+1, c'(log_2 H)^{0.6309}} for H>=32 (chain lemma L1, two-children-below-depth-2 lemma L2, binary-subtree lemma L3; the first, Theta(log H), term is dominant) — answer:work:006-lower-bound-v5-compact. SANITY CHECKS AND FAILURE MODES (D7/D9): labeled hand-checkable observations O1-O3 ((1,1,1,3), (1,1,3,11), (1,3,11,131) with parent-edge values d'=1,1,1 and one-line substitutions); two recorded induction/proof failure modes that were caught and corrected (the false mod-3 obstruction route; the false d_j >= 11(2+sqrt3)^{j-2} skeleton inequality); one corrected false dominance clause in the lower-bound packet. REPORTED OBSTRUCTION: the bounded d<=100 cross-checking enumeration (fully specified, reproducible procedure frozen in question:work:005-exception-search-v4) never executed — three attempts all failed on output-length overruns (blocked, zero-evidence answers answer:work:005-exception-search-v4 and predecessors), so empirical corroboration is limited to the labeled spot checks; this is an execution gap, not a mathematical one, since D1-D3 are proved unconditionally. CONJECTURES, STRICTLY SEPARATED (D8): (i) exponent sharpness — is rho = ln3/ln11 improvable toward the true growth, e.g. via the sketched-but-unexecuted iterated product-jump dichotomy (product-raising children jump p -> >= p^{3/2}, potentially yielding N(H) = O_eps(H^eps)) — open as question:raised:07d805ce56d7:rq-sharp; (ii) lower side beyond Theta(log H) — requires a positive-density two-child branching lemma with average log-growth slope strictly below 3 — open as question:raised:529a9c7e8677:rq-d5-stronger. No growth law is assumed anywhere; the proved bracket is c*log H <= N(H) <= C*H^{0.4582} + O(log H). MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT MATHEMATICAL STEP: quantify typical branching and typical per-edge factor inside one fast subtree subtree(u_j) (rq-sharp), or equivalently prove the positive-density branching lemma on the lower side (rq-d5-stronger); a cheap auxiliary step is hand-executing the frozen d<=100 enumeration spec. Acceptance is met as honest partial progress with complete proofs of the structural claims and explicit, effective quantitative bounds, per the dossier's stated standard.

selected_packets.account:
MEMORANDUM — structural core (D1–D3) for S = {sorted 1≤a≤b≤c≤d, a²+b²+c²+d²=4abcd}, mutation x↦4·(product of others)−x then re-sort; root (1,1,1,1); height h(v)=d (decision 4). All proved from definitions SC1–SC2; no external materials exist (SC6).

LEMMA V (Vieta conjugate). If (a,b,c,d)∈S then d′=4abc−d is an integer ≥1 and (a,b,c,d′), re-sorted, lies in S. Proof: d is a root of t²−4abc·t+(a²+b²+c²)=0; the other root d′ has d+d′=4abc∈ℤ and dd′=a²+b²+c²>0, so d′∈ℤ and d′≥1; the equation gives a²+b²+c²+d′²=4abc·d′. ∎

LEMMA L2 (top tie only at root). If c=d then v=(1,1,1,1). Proof: the equation gives a²+b²=(4ab−2)d². Since ab≥1, RHS≥2d²; since a,b≤d, LHS≤2d². Equality: 4ab−2=2 ⇒ ab=1 ⇒ a=b=1, and 2=2d² ⇒ d=1. (Same as the suggested route: d² | a²+b² forces a²+b²∈{d²,2d²}; the first gives 4ab=3, impossible; the second is above.) Hence at every non-root vertex c<d: the maximum coordinate is unique; also a=d⇒c=d⇒root. ∎

LEMMA L1 (descent). At every non-root v: 1≤d′<d. Proof: d′≥1 by Lemma V. Assume d′≥d. Then d²≤dd′=a²+b²+c²≤3c², so d≤c√3. Then 4abc²≤4abcd=a²+b²+c²+d²≤2(a²+b²+c²)≤6c², hence 4ab≤6, i.e. 2ab≤3, so ab=1 and a=b=1. Now d²≤a²+b²+c²=c²+2<(c+1)² (since 2<2c+1 for c≥1), so d≤c; with d≥c, d=c. The equation becomes 2+2c²=4c², so c=1 and v=(1,1,1,1) — contradiction. ∎ Note: no Pell/mod-3 step is needed; the previously suggested exclusion of m²=3c²−2 mod 3 is invalid as stated (m²≡1 mod 3 occurs, e.g. c=1), and this route avoids it entirely.

LEMMA L3 (mutating below the max grows, factor ≥3). At non-root v, mutate x∈{a,b,c}: x′=4(abcd/x)−x≥4d−d=3d>d, because the other three coordinates include d (product ≥d) and x≤d. After re-sorting the new maximum is x′ (other entries ≤d<x′). So every mutation not at d strictly increases height, by factor ≥3 (for x=c the factor is ≥4ab−1). ∎

COROLLARY (no height-preserving mutation; the d-mutation lowers height). At non-root v: mutating d yields re-sorted (a,b,c,d′) with max=max(c,d′)<d (d′<d by L1, c<d by L2); mutating a,b,c yields max≥3d>d by L3. Hence every mutation strictly changes height. At the root the unique mutated vertex is (1,1,1,3), height 3>1. ∎

THEOREM D2 (unique height-decreasing mutation). At every non-root v exactly one mutated vertex has height<h(v): the one from mutating the maximum coordinate d; all other coordinate-mutations raise height to ≥3d. Uniqueness is at the level of vertices of the quotient (sorted) graph: if a=b or b=c, some of the four coordinate-mutations coincide after sorting (mutating a vs b when a=b gives the same multiset), but all such coincidences lie among height-increasing mutations, so the height-decreasing vertex is unique; since c<d (L2) it also comes from a unique coordinate index. No mutation fixes height. ∎

THEOREM D1 (connectivity). Define parent(v), v≠root: mutate at d, re-sort. By the Corollary h(parent(v))=max(c,d′)<d=h(v); by Lemma V parent(v)∈S. Iterating, height is a strictly decreasing positive integer, reaching 1 within d−1 steps; height 1 forces (1,1,1,1) (since 1≤a≤b≤c≤d=1), and (1,1,1,1)∈S as 1+1+1+1=4=4·1·1·1·1. So every v∈S is joined to the root by a mutation path. ∎

THEOREM D3 (rooted tree). The mutation relation on S is symmetric — coordinate mutation x↦M−x is an involution — so the quotient graph on sorted vertices is undirected. It is connected (D1). It is acyclic: in any cycle take a vertex v of maximal height; its two distinct cycle-neighbors have height≤h(v), cannot exceed h(v) (maximality), and cannot equal it (Corollary), so both are height-decreasing mutations of v — contradicting D2. Connected and acyclic ⇒ tree, rooted at (1,1,1,1) with parent as in D1; a multiple parent (a second lower-height neighbor) would contradict D2 identically. ∎

LABELED OBSERVATIONS (hand-checkable spot checks, reproducible by direct substitution; not an enumeration): O1: (1,1,1,3): 1+1+1+9=12=4·3; d′=4−3=1, parent is root; all four root-mutations give 3, so the root has exactly one child. O2: (1,1,3,11): 1+1+9+121=132=4·33; d′=4·3−11=1, parent (1,1,1,3); mutating c=3 gives 41: (1,1,11,41), max 41≥3·11 (L3 confirmed). O3: (1,3,11,131): 1+9+121+17161=17292=4·4323, from (1,1,3,11) by mutating a 1 (4·1·3·11−1=131); d′=4·3·11−131=1, parent (1,1,3,11). Hence (1,1,3,11) has exactly two children (mutating a vs b coincide since a=b): branching exists and the equal-coordinate subtlety is realized already at depth 2.

STATUS: D1, D2, D3 PROVED, no counterexamples, no induction failure modes (L1 covers every non-root vertex; termination uses only that height is a positive integer). No growth law is assumed or implied; D4–D8 belong to the sibling threads.

claims.statement: Vieta conjugate lemma: for (a,b,c,d) in S, d' = 4abc-d is an integer >= 1 and the re-sorted tuple (a,b,c,d') is again in S; mutation is an involution at the coordinate level, so the sorted mutation graph is undirected.

L2: c=d occurs only at the root (1,1,1,1). Proof: a^2+b^2=(4ab-2)d^2 is simultaneously >= 2d^2 (ab>=1) and <= 2d^2 (a,b<=d), forcing ab=1, a=b=1, then 2=2d^2, d=1. Consequently every non-root vertex has a unique maximum coordinate (c<d), and a=d only at the root.

counterevidence: The mod-3/Pell obstruction suggested in the work:001 prompt (m^2=3c^2-2 impossible mod 3) is false as stated: m^2 = 3c^2-2 ≡ 1 (mod 3), which is a possible residue (c=1 gives m=1). The present route needs no such exclusion.
claims.statement: L1 (descent): at every non-root vertex, 1 <= d' = 4abc-d < d. Proof: d'>=1 by cV; assuming d'>=d gives d^2<=a^2+b^2+c^2<=3c^2, then 4abc^2<=4abcd<=2(a^2+b^2+c^2)<=6c^2, so 2ab<=3, a=b=1; then d^2<=c^2+2<(c+1)^2 forces d=c, and 2+2c^2=4c^2 gives c=1, i.e. the root — contradiction.

L3: at a non-root vertex, mutating any coordinate x in {a,b,c} gives x' = 4(abcd/x) - x >= 4d - d = 3d > d (the other three coordinates include d, so their product is >= d, and x <= d); after re-sorting the new maximum is x' >= 3d. For x=c the factor is >= 4ab-1.

Corollary: no mutation preserves the maximum. At a non-root vertex, mutating d strictly lowers the maximum to max(c,d') < d (by cL1 and cL2); mutating a, b, or c raises it to >= 3d (by cL3). At the root the unique mutation raises height 1 to 3.

D2 PROVED: every non-root vertex has a unique height-decreasing mutation as a vertex of the sorted (quotient) graph — the mutation at the maximum coordinate d; all other coordinate-mutations raise the height to >= 3d, and none preserves it. Equal coordinates (a=b or b=c) can make height-increasing coordinate-mutations coincide after sorting, but never affect uniqueness of the height-decreasing one; since c<d at non-roots, that mutation also comes from a unique coordinate index.

D1 PROVED: iterating parent(v) = (mutate at d, re-sort) strictly decreases the positive integer height, so it reaches height 1 within d-1 steps; the only sorted quadruple with d=1 is (1,1,1,1), which satisfies the equation (4=4). Hence every solution is connected to the root by a mutation path.

D3 PROVED: the quotient mutation graph is a rooted tree. Undirected by the involution property (cV); connected by D1; acyclic because a cycle's maximal-height vertex would have two distinct height-decreasing neighbors, contradicting D2 (heights equal to the maximum are excluded by cCor); multiple parents excluded by the same argument. Parent map as in D1 makes the tree canonical.

Labeled observations (hand-checkable substitution spot checks, not an enumeration): (1,1,1,3): 1+1+1+9=12=4*3, d'=1 so parent is the root, and the root has exactly one child; (1,1,3,11): 1+1+9+121=132=4*33, d'=1, mutating c gives (1,1,11,41) with 41>=3*11; (1,3,11,131): 1+9+121+17161=17292=4*4323, child of (1,1,3,11) via mutating a 1, d'=1. So (1,1,3,11) has exactly two children: branching exists, and the a=b mutation-coincidence occurs already at depth 2.

counterevidence: The previously suggested mod-3 exclusion route (m^2 = 3c^2 - 2 impossible mod 3) is false as stated — m^2 ≡ 1 (mod 3) is possible; recorded so the flawed route is not resurrected. The proof here bypasses it.
Re-sorting concern checked: the conjugate d' may exceed c (parent's remaining entries reorder), but max(parent) = max(c, d') < d regardless, so descent is unaffected.
No counterexample to D1, D2, or D3 was found; all three are proved, so the failure-structure branch of the demand (exhibit a component, cycle, or multiple parent) is vacuous.

selected_packets.objective: Prove D1-D3 compactly for S = {sorted quadruples 1<=a<=b<=c<=d, a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd} under Vieta mutation (x_i -> 4*(product of others) - x_i, then re-sort), with root (1,1,1,1). REQUIRED ROUTE (verify, fix, or replace, but keep it elementary): (L1, descent) at any non-root vertex the conjugate d' = 4abc - d = (a^2+b^2+c^2)/d is an integer >= 1; prove d' < d by contradiction: d' >= d gives a^2+b^2+c^2 >= d^2, and combined with a^2+b^2+c^2 <= 3c^2 gives d <= c*sqrt(3); feeding into the equation gives 2ab <= 3, hence a=b=1; then 2+c^2+d^2 = 4cd with c <= d <= 3c/2 forces c=1 and d=1, i.e. the root - contradiction. (L2) c = d only at the root: from a^2+b^2+2d^2 = 4abd^2 deduce d^2 | a^2+b^2 and a^2+b^2 <= 2d^2, so a^2+b^2 in {d^2, 2d^2}; the first gives 3=4ab (impossible), the second gives ab=1 and then d=1. (L3) mutating any coordinate strictly below the maximum strictly increases the maximum: new value >= 4ab d - d >= 3d > d since ab >= 1 (and a=d only at root by L2-type argument). Conclude: (D2) the mutation at the unique maximal coordinate is the unique height-decreasing mutation, i.e. strictly decreases d; (D1) iterating it strictly decreases the positive integer d, so every vertex descends to d=1, and the only vertex with d=1 is (1,1,1,1) - verify this endpoint claim; (D3) the quotient graph is a rooted tree: a cycle's maximal-height vertex would have two distinct height-decreasing mutations, contradicting D2; multiple parents likewise. Address explicitly the subtlety that equal coordinates (a=b or b=c) make some of the 4 coordinate-mutations coincide after sorting, so 'unique height-decreasing mutation' is a statement about distinct mutated vertices, not coordinate indices. KEEP THE ANSWER COMPACT (target well under 1200 words): lemma - proof format, no digressions, no worked tables beyond at most 3 one-line substitution checks. If any lemma fails, stop and report the verified counterexample instead.

T1 (depth upper). Each child edge multiplies the max by >= 3, so d >= 3^{depth(v)} and depth(v) <= log_3 d.

T2 (crude count). N(H) <= sum_{0<=k<=floor(log_3 H)} 3^k = (3^{floor(log_3 H)+1} - 1)/2 <= (3H-1)/2. N(H) = O(H), constant 3/2.

T3 (depth lower). Child max = 4*(product of other three) - x <= 4bcd <= 4d^3. Let L_k = max of log_2 d at depth k: L_{k+1} <= 3L_k + 2, L_0 = 0, so L_k + 1 <= 3(L_{k-1} + 1), giving L_k <= 3^k - 1. Hence depth(v) >= log_3(log_2 d + 1). Two-sided: log_3(log_2 d + 1) <= depth(v) <= log_3 d.

T4 (rq1 dichotomy; Outcome A holds). (i) The a=b=1 locus is a single chain. Equation: 2 + c^2 + d^2 = 4cd. The parent of (1,1,c,d) is the re-sorted (1,1,c,d'), d' = (c^2+2)/d < d, again with a=b=1; descending to the root and inverting gives the chain v_0=(1,1,1,1), v_1=(1,1,1,3), v_{j+1} = (1,1,d_j,4d_j - c_j) with c_{j+1}=d_j, i.e. d_{j+1} = 4d_j - d_{j-1}, ratio r_j = 4 - 1/r_{j-1} increasing from r_1 = 11/3 toward 2+sqrt(3). Chain vertices with d <= H: O(log H). For j >= 2 (c_j >= 3), v_j has exactly 2 children: v_{j+1} and u_j; every a=b=1 vertex lies on this chain.

(ii) ab is nondecreasing along child edges. Mutating x in {a,b,c}: x' > d is the new max, so the child's two smallest entries are the two smallest of {a,b,c,d}\{x}: mutate a gives bc >= ab; mutate b gives ac >= ab; mutate c leaves ab.

(iii) The unique off-chain child of v_j (j >= 2) is u_j = (1,c_j,d_j,4c_jd_j - 1), max m_j = 4c_jd_j - 1 >= 12d_j - 1 >= 11d_j; its ab = c_j >= 3, so by (ii) every vertex of subtree(u_j) has ab >= 3 and every edge below multiplies the max by >= 4ab - 1 >= 11. The subtrees subtree(u_j), j >= 2, are pairwise disjoint (tree, distinct parents), disjoint from the chain (there b >= 3), and every vertex lies on the chain or in exactly one of them (descend to the root; the path leaves the chain at most once, since ab >= 3 is irreversible by (ii)).

(iv) Subtree count. Vertices of subtree(u_j) with max <= H sit at depth <= log_{11}(H/m_j) below u_j, <= 3 children each, so size <= sum_k 3^k <= (3/2)*3^{log_{11}(H/m_j)} = (3/2)(H/m_j)^rho with rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582 < 1/2.

Hence sum_{j>=2} m_j^{-rho} <= 121^{-rho} / (1 - (11/3)^{-rho}) = 0.248, convergent since (11/3)^rho = 1.814 > 1. Therefore N(H) <= C*H^rho + O(log H), rho = ln3/ln11 = 0.4582, C = (3/2)*sum_{j>=2} m_j^{-rho} <= 0.372, an effective constant. N(H) = O(H^{0.4582}), sublinear; rq1 resolved by Outcome A.

context.title: Markov-Hurwitz equation a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd: Vieta-mutation graph structure and growth of N(H)
